C0.quote: pairwise comparisons capture the majority relation between pairs of candidates
C0.note: Tournament solutions (winner selection from pairwise majority relations) and margin of victory, which has a bribery/manipulation interpretation; treated as a voting-rule paper.

C1.quote: using axiomatic and probabilistic analysis (Section 3) as well as through experiments (Section 4)
C1.note: Main results are structural/axiomatic (cover-consistency, degree-consistency) plus a probabilistic theorem. Experiments are on synthetic tournaments (SI). MoV is interpreted as bribery cost (SB), but no strategic analysis is performed. SB is included only weakly.

C2.1.quote: pairwise comparisons capture the majority relation between pairs of candidates

C2.2.quote: A tournament T = (V, E) is a directed graph in which exactly one directed edge exists

C2.3.note: Voters and their preferences are not modelled. Preferences appear only as a generator for random tournaments in the experiments.

C2.4.quote: represents an asymmetric and connex dominance relation between the alternatives
C2.4.note: The input is only the tournament. No held attitude is referred to.

C3.1.note: Edge reversals are used only to define MoV, not as strategic voter behaviour.

C4.1.note: No utility-type notion is used for voters.

C5.1.note: The criteria evaluated are consistency with the covering relation, degree-consistency and discriminative power. Pareto optimality is mentioned only in the Discussion.

VOT.note: No voter agents in the model.

BRI.note: The bribery interpretation is mentioned in the introduction. No briber acts in the model; reversal sets are a combinatorial definition.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

C9.1.note: The introduction mentions the bribery and manipulation interpretation, and the discussion suggests max-MoV_UC as a new tournament solution. These are weak, rule-level claims about the rule's structural and discriminative properties, not about institutions, voters' welfare or which rule should be used in practice.

C10.1.note: No statement about procedural reading or about the relation between inputs and held attitudes.
